title: Toy Story 5 Hits Indian Theaters Next Thursday. The Rest of the Summer Doesn't Stand a Chance.
excerpt: Jessie finally takes the spotlight as Pixar's biggest franchise battles a tablet for the soul of playtime — with a projected $165 million US opening and a same-day Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu release.
body:
There's a moment in the Toy Story 5 trailer where Woody looks at Buzz Lightyear with the expression of a man who's been through four movies of existential crises and still isn't sure he's processing any of it correctly. It lasts about two seconds. It's perfect. And it's a reminder that Pixar, when it decides to show up, still knows how to make you feel things you didn't consent to feeling.

The fifth installment of the franchise that basically invented modern animation arrives in Indian theaters on June 19 — in English, Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu. That same-day multilingual release is Pixar's clearest signal yet that India isn't an afterthought market. It's a priority.

And the numbers back it up. According to early tracking, Toy Story 5 is eyeing a $145 to $165 million opening weekend in the US alone, which would make it the biggest opening of 2026 — eclipsing The Super Mario Galaxy Movie's $131 million debut and smashing the franchise record set by Toy Story 4 at $120.9 million. That film went on to earn $1.07 billion worldwide. The fifth is projected even higher.

Directed by Andrew Stanton — the Academy Award-winning mind behind WALL-E and Finding Nemo — the new film shifts focus from Woody's perpetual identity crisis to Jessie, the cowgirl who's been scene-stealing since Toy Story 2 and finally gets the spotlight she deserves. Joan Cusack returns to voice her, and from the trailers, it's clear Stanton has built the emotional architecture of this film around her fierce loyalty and abandonment fears.

The antagonist — if you can call her that — is Lilypad, a sentient tablet device voiced by Greta Lee (Past Lives). She arrives in Bonnie's room with her own ideas about what children need, and suddenly every toy in the house is redundant. It's Toy Story doing what it does best: using plastic cowboys and space rangers to gut-punch you with questions about relevance, obsolescence, and whether love is enough when the world moves on.

The voice cast is stacked beyond reason. Tom Hanks returns as Woody. Tim Allen is back as Buzz. Conan O'Brien voices a character called Smarty Pants, which feels like a role he was born for. Craig Robinson plays a talking GPS hippo toy named Atlas. Keanu Reeves returns as Duke Caboom. Annie Potts is back as Bo Peep. And Scarlett Spears voices Bonnie at age eight, which means the kid from Toy Story 4 has grown up — and so have the stakes.

For Indian audiences, the Hindi dubbed version has already generated serious buzz, with Disney India pushing the regional-language releases hard across social media. The "toys versus tech" theme resonates differently in a country where smartphone penetration among children has skyrocketed — every Indian parent who's handed their toddler an iPad during a restaurant dinner is going to feel personally seen by this film's premise.

"The toys are back — and this time, their jobs are challenged."

For NRI families in the US and Canada, Toy Story 5 is already shaping up to be the defining family outing of the summer. It opens the same week as Cocktail 2 in India, which means Bollywood's biggest romantic drama and Pixar's biggest animated sequel will be competing for the same weekend audience. That's a box office clash worth watching.

The original Toy Story released in 1995. Thirty-one years later, the franchise is still the gold standard for animated storytelling. If the projections hold, Toy Story 5 won't just be the biggest opening of 2026 — it could push the franchise past $4 billion in cumulative global earnings.

Jessie's waited a long time for this. So have we.

Toy Story 5 releases in Indian theaters on June 19 in English, Hindi, Tamil, and Telugu.
author: Diaspora Desk
